questions.question: If oil and water build up in your vehicle's air tanks, the brakes:
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks stops brakes from working properly.

questions.question: If you don't keep the fifth wheel plate greased, it could:
questions.explanation: Without proper grease on the fifth wheel plate, friction builds up between the tractor and trailer. This causes steering problems.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before every trip. Pull out the trailer air supply control and move the tractor forward slightly. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: Rollovers happen most often when:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn too fast. Slow down before turning, especially with a full load.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure, it will:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. Loss of air pressure in this line will activate the emergency brakes on the trailer.

questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for escaping air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Wait for air pressure to build. Open the shut-off valves on the last trailer. If air escapes, the entire vehicle has air pressure.

questions.question: Starting in what year did new trailers have to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers made after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: Look into the back of the fifth wheel to make sure the jaws are properly closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: Before backing under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are:
questions.explanation: Before backing under the trailer when coupling, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, the valve will pop out when:

options.text: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
Wheels regain traction after a skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line. It carries air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents.
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:

options.text: A truck driver is driving too fast.
The driver in front of a truck is moving too slowly.
A truck driver is driving too slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: A truck driver is driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a vehicle is driven too fast. To reduce rollover risk, load cargo low and centered. Take turns and curves slowly.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to turn over.
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: A combination vehicle has:
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle goes around a corner:

options.text: The turn should be made as tightly as possible.
The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
The rear wheels should run over the curb.
It is acceptable to knock over street signs if they are too close to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear wheels move in different paths.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking. This effect is more pronounced on vehicles with trailers.

questions.question: Emergency air lines are often coded with the color:
questions.explanation: Service air line parts are usually coded blue. Emergency air line parts are usually coded red.
